findings.trigger: Two separate Windows worktrees share one Godot binary directory; second runner starts after the first runner snapshots process IDs.
findings.observed: Mutex is scoped by PSScriptRoot, while Windows process owner is inferred from Godot executable directory and not-in-baseline PID. Stop-NewGodotProcesses can terminate the other worktree's process.
findings.expected: Only stop verified invocation-owned processes, never another worktree's Godot.

evidence.fact: Per-worktree mutex does not synchronize other worktrees
Windows process enumeration filters by shared executable directory
New-process cleanup can kill any later process from shared directory
Cleanup follows test completion

established_facts: Per-worktree mutex does not synchronize other worktrees
Windows process enumeration filters by shared executable directory
New-process cleanup can kill any later process from shared directory
Cleanup follows test completion
findings.assumptions_or_unproved: No actual cross-worktree kill was induced. This is a source-reachable conditional runner bug, not a gameplay failure.
findings.minimal_fix: Use Windows Job Object or invocation-owned PID lineage/creation evidence; remove executable-directory-only kill eligibility.
findings.minimum_validation: Isolated two-worktree concurrent fake/native process test with same engine directory; confirm foreign PID survives and own descendants are released.

findings.function: Windows source and engine admission / framework receipt
findings.trigger: A Windows framework run has no populated HARDCORE_R3_CONTENT_SHA256 or otherwise lacks verified exact source/engine input fingerprint.
findings.observed: Linux validates source-fingerprint format and engine version, but Windows skips those preconditions; Test-FrameworkReceipt compares source only when expected is nonempty. Runner aggregate stores git_head but not exact dirty/input/engine hashes.
findings.expected: Release-grade native evidence requires exact actual source, engine, scene/input, invocation, receipt and producer binding; a missing hash must be visible as unbound.
findings.owner: Formal test runner and receipt admission

established_facts: Source fingerprint/engine version preflight inside Linux branch
ExpectedContentSha256 defaults to empty
Source comparison skipped when expected empty
Windows checks scene/run/invocation but no matching strict engine fingerprint
Structured aggregate git_head does not bind all dirty input bytes
findings.assumptions_or_unproved: External 50/51/52 freezes supplement native binding; this does not invalidate their verified limited scopes.
findings.minimal_fix: Make missing source/engine/scene fingerprints fail closed for formal evidence, or mark unbound; continue using separately verified immutable freeze ledgers.
findings.minimum_validation: Receipt-only missing/mismatch/valid fingerprint negative and positive cases; do not repeat unchanged suite solely for this audit.

findings.trigger: Multiple combat_epoch_delivery attempts sequentially call finish with the same output name.
findings.observed: FileAccess.WRITE overwrites one fixed output JSON path with latest check list, without attempt/run ID or preserved old blob. Committed stage50 full custom list is absent; stage50 native FAIL/stdout remain, stage51 and52 lists are retained.
findings.expected: Every attempt's custom assertion list must remain immutable and bound to its own native exit, not overwritten by a later PASS.

findings.assumptions_or_unproved: The missing stage50 itemized check list cannot be reconstructed from stdout marker counts.
findings.minimal_fix: Allocate per-attempt output directory with run/invocation ID and append-only immutable archive before next producer; preserve historical missing status.
findings.minimum_validation: Disposable sequence fail->pass same scene, verify both exact check arrays and associated native_result; never manufacture lost50 check list.

findings.expected: Functional PASS and cleanup warnings should be separately visible, without automatically treating each headless renderer warning as a production memory leak.

findings.function: Windows test appdata, log, evidence override paths
findings.trigger: Windows runner invoked with untrusted/accidental HARDCORE_AUDIT_RUNTIME_APPDATA or HARDCORE_AUDIT_LOG_ROOT referencing outside checkout or a reparse-point.
findings.observed: External overrides are accepted and used to create directories; log files are removed prior to scene, and APPDATA is set, but physical containment/link validation only runs on Linux.
findings.expected: Normal test cannot read/write real player saves or unrelated workspaces; path overrides need explicit owned namespace policy.
